citation: 'Ruins, St. Michael's Church', wood engraving (Blomgren Bros., Chicago), in A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 2 (Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885), p. 405.
author: Blomgren Bros., engravers, Chicago (signed at lower left)
describes_date: October 1871, the church's walls standing after the fire
repository: Internet Archive, item historyofchicago02andr (printed page 405). The engraving is committed at data/sources/assets/landmarks_1871_t3689/andreas_v2_p405_st_michaels_ruins.jpg.
locator: Vol. 2, p. 405, the engraving beside the account of St. Michael's parish: the burnt-out church from the north-west, across Linden Street; the broken tower on the front's east corner, the nave gable with its round window, the west aisle's gable and a pinnacled corner buttress, the Hurlbut Street side running away to the right; bare trees and brick rubble in the foreground.
rights_note: Published 1885 in the United States; public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-20 (T-3689) from the Internet Archive's page image of p. 405 (2306 x 3299 px); the engraving cropped and committed at 1140 x 1035 px, sha256 4fd37a22d50669a2e3c4b5bd83a3ae7179046a17c49dd6835f6240ab8b58b36a.
note: Drawn for the 1885 history, most likely from a photograph of the ruins. It shows what stood after the fire: the walls, without roof, steeple or glass.
what_it_supplies: the church's front and west side, and the tower's place on the front's east corner
the walls' heights against the church's 80-foot width
that the walls stood after the fire
what_it_does_not_supply: the roof, the steeple and the bells (burned)
the east side and the rear
